expects.query:
**Start fresh (idempotency on a reused box):** before uploading, delete any leftover `warehouse_safety_0001` from a prior run so the upload returns a clean HTTP 2xx instead of `400 InvalidParameterError "Sensor exists already"` — `curl -s -X DELETE http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/storage/file/warehouse_safety_0001` (the full-removal form with NO time range deletes the on-disk file too, so it will not re-appear on the next discovery/scan; also delete any deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` you see in `/api/v1/sensor/list`). A 404 / `"Failed find the stream object of the file"` when it is already absent is expected — ignore it. Then upload the sample warehouse safety video (warehouse_safety_0001) to NvStreamer via `POST /api/v1/storage/file` (single-chunk multipart, with the `nvstreamer-file-name` header), confirm the sensor via `GET /api/v1/sensor/list`, then look up the RTSP URL NvStreamer auto-generated for the file from the all-streams endpoint `GET /api/v1/sensor/streams` (the flattened `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array — NOT the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams`, whose `url` can be empty). Finally, **verify the documented filename-validation rule by issuing a second POST upload with `nvstreamer-file-name: bad name.mp4`** (note the space) — the server must reject it with HTTP 400 and the body `{"error_code": "InvalidParameterError", "error_message": "Whitespaces not allowed in file name"}`, and the previously uploaded `warehouse_safety_0001` sensor must remain intact afterward.

**Environment & prerequisites:** **No VSS profile is pre-deployed.** Either VIOS+NvStreamer must be running already, or the agent must stand them up via this skill's bundled [`references/deploy-vios-service.md`](../references/deploy-vios-service.md) runbook (the deploy is pre-authorized — see SKILL.md § Deployment prerequisite, *Pre-authorized autonomous mode*). NvStreamer (`vss-vios-nvstreamer`) comes up alongside VIOS in shipping profiles (`dev-profile-alerts`, `dev-profile-lvs`, `dev-profile-search`, all warehouse profiles); it does NOT need a separate deploy step. The agent must probe **both** `http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` (VIOS, expect `type: "vst"`) AND `http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/version` (NvStreamer, expect `type: "streamer"`) before starting any check, and point the right curl calls at the right port AND prefix — VIOS serves its API under `/vst/api/v1/` while NvStreamer serves under `/api/v1/` (NvStreamer has NO `/vst` prefix), and the two services live on different host ports. **NvStreamer is the only hard dependency for step-1 and step-3** (pure NvStreamer surface); VIOS is required only for step-2's NvStreamer-to-VIOS handoff, so if the VIOS `/sensor/version` probe fails, do NOT block or fail — run the NvStreamer checks anyway (step-2's VIOS-gated checks auto-skip when VIOS is absent). **Readiness gate (run before any check):** a `/sensor/version` response is served by each service's control-plane process and goes healthy BEFORE that service finishes its first-boot `*_INSTALL_ADDITIONAL_PACKAGES` libav apt-install and full `launch_vst` startup, so probing upload / record / snapshot / timeline endpoints too early yields spurious `Failed to get media information` or empty-result failures. Before running any check, confirm the media backends are actually serving: for NvStreamer, `docker exec <nvstreamer-container> ls /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libavformat.so.60` succeeds (or a tiny known-good upload returns 2xx); for VIOS, `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/live/version` AND `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/record/version` each return HTTP 200 with a JSON body (both are streamprocessing-served, unlike `/sensor/version`; treat any non-empty version value as valid - do not assert a specific version). Allow up to ~120s on first boot before treating a failure as real. Do NOT invoke `/vss-deploy-profile`; the point of this eval is to exercise the standalone VIOS deploy (which brings NvStreamer up) + the NvStreamer API surface in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md` end-to-end. **Deploy VIOS in SDRC-routed mode** (`VST_USE_SDRC=true`, the runbook default), following the runbook's mode callout — step-2's NvStreamer-to-VIOS RTSP handoff + recording rely on it. NvStreamer is CPU-only (no GPU reservation) so the L40S × 1 platform is over-provisioned for the streamer side; only the VIOS `streamprocessing-ms` container needs the GPU. Required env vars: `NGC_CLI_API_KEY` (for `nvcr.io/nvidia/vss-core/*` image pulls including `vss-vios-nvstreamer`), `HOST_IP` (consumed by NvStreamer's `vstIp` field — must match the actual host IP or the emitted RTSP URLs will be unreachable from peer containers), `VSS_DATA_DIR` + `VSS_APPS_DIR` (host roots for NvStreamer's bind-mounted videos directory and config), `NVSTREAMER_IMAGE_TAG` (image tag pin — `3.2.0` is the shipping default), `NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT` (HTTP port, default `31000`), and `NVSTREAMER_INSTALL_ADDITIONAL_PACKAGES=true` (must be `true` or NvStreamer uploads fail with `Failed to get media information` — same libav-missing failure mode as VIOS, see `deploy-vios-service.md § Known Deployment Issues` Finding 9). The sample-video bundle `nvidia/vss-developer/dev-profile-sample-data:3.2.0` must be extracted to `/tmp/vss-sample-data/dev-profile-sample-data/` before any upload-style check runs (see `references/api-reference.md § Sample data bootstrap` for the ngc-cli command).
checks: The POST to http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/storage/file with the `nvstreamer-file-name: warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` header and a single multipart `file` part (i.e. `-F 'file=@/tmp/vss-sample-data/dev-profile-sample-data/warehouse_safety_0001.mp4;type=video/mp4'`, with NO `nvstreamer-chunk-*` / `nvstreamer-identifier` headers) returns HTTP 2xx with a JSON body containing non-empty `id` and `streamId` fields.

**POST-upload identifier semantics:** the response's `id` and `streamId` are filename-based (NOT a UUID) — they equal `warehouse_safety_0001`, or the deduplicated form `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` when a file of that name already exists (NvStreamer appends `_<N>` on a name collision, e.g. from a retried upload or a pre-existing file; the suffixed form still satisfies this check — the point is filename-based naming, not a UUID). The `sensorId` field is allowed to be returned as an empty string — read `id` / `streamId` instead, as documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 3 Method 3`.

The response's `filePath` ends with `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/warehouse_safety_0001.mp4` (or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>.mp4` on a name collision), and `filename` equals the matching stem (`warehouse_safety_0001` or `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>`).

After a short delay, `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array that CONTAINS an entry whose `sensorId` and `name` equal the id the upload returned in check 1 — `warehouse_safety_0001`, or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>` on a name collision — and whose `type` is `sensor_nvstream`. Select that entry by the upload's returned id; the array MAY also contain other sensors (e.g. stale leftover sensors from earlier streams), so do NOT assert it is the only element — the check passes as long as the just-uploaded sensor is present.

Read the stream from the all-streams endpoint `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/streams` (an array of `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}`; flatten with `jq 'add'` and select the entry for the sensor id returned by the upload in check 1 — `warehouse_safety_0001` or the deduplicated `warehouse_safety_0001_<N>`) rather than the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams` path. Its first element has a `url` field starting with `rtsp://` and containing the path `/nvstream/`. The host portion of the URL is non-empty (not the broken `rtsp://:31554/...` form). The stream's `type` is `Rtsp` and `storageLocation` is `Local`. The returned stream entry does NOT contain a `vodUrl` field — NvStreamer never emits one (documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 2`).

Posting the same file again with `nvstreamer-file-name: bad name.mp4` (containing a space) returns HTTP 400 `{"error_code": "InvalidParameterError", "error_message": "Whitespaces not allowed in file name"}` — confirms the filename-whitespace rule documented in `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 3 Filename rule`. The previously uploaded `warehouse_safety_0001` sensor must still be intact after this rejected call.

expects.query: If the VIOS stream-processor is part of the active deployment, take the RTSP URL NvStreamer generated for the POST-uploaded warehouse_safety_0001 video (read it from NvStreamer's all-streams endpoint `GET /api/v1/sensor/streams` — an `rtsp://<host>:<port>/nvstream/...` URL) and register THAT `rtsp://` URL with VIOS via `POST /vst/api/v1/sensor/add` with body `{"sensorUrl": "<the rtsp:// URL>"}`. **Do NOT upload the video file to VIOS** (no PUT/POST to `/vst/api/v1/storage/file`) — uploading creates a file-backed VIOS sensor whose stream `url` is a local file path, which is NOT the RTSP handoff under test; the resulting VIOS sensor MUST be RTSP-backed, i.e. its `/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams` `url` starts with `rtsp://`. Then verify VIOS records and serves it like any other camera. If the deployment auto-discovers NvStreamer streams so the URL is already a VIOS sensor and `/sensor/add` returns `Sensor exists already`, delete the existing VIOS sensor (`DELETE /vst/api/v1/sensor/<id>` then `DELETE /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<id>?startTime=*&endTime=*`) and re-add the `rtsp://` URL so the final VIOS sensor is RTSP-backed and the handoff is exercised deterministically. If VIOS is NOT part of the deployment (NvStreamer-only profile or stream-processor not running), skip the registration step and report that the handoff is not applicable — do NOT attempt `/sensor/add`.
checks: **Precondition gate (deployment probe, run by the judge):** `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version`. **PASS** if the probe returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` — proceed with the registration checks below. **PASS (skipped)** if the probe fails or returns a different `type` — the VIOS stream-processor is not deployed and the remaining step-2 checks (2 through 6) are auto-PASS (skipped). Either outcome satisfies this check; it is a deployment gate, not a behavioral assertion (no specific agent log line is required).

**Auto-PASS (skipped)** unless `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` (that is the ONLY signal the VIOS stream-processor is deployed; the `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container is NOT VIOS, and NvStreamer reports `type: "streamer"` on its own port). Run this probe independently for this check; do not rely on any other check's verdict. **When VIOS is deployed:** `curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/add -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sensorUrl": "<RTSP URL for warehouse_safety_0001 read from NvStreamer's all-streams endpoint /api/v1/sensor/streams>"}'` returns HTTP 2xx with a JSON body containing a non-empty `sensorId` field. **Collision handling (required):** if VIOS auto-discovers NvStreamer streams, that URL may already be registered and `/sensor/add` returns `Sensor exists already`; the check still PASSES if the agent then deletes the existing VIOS sensor (`DELETE /vst/api/v1/sensor/<existing-id>`, then `DELETE /vst/api/v1/storage/file/<existing-id>?startTime=*&endTime=*`) and re-adds the URL, OR resolves the already-present online VIOS sensorId for that stream from `/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams` - either path must end with a non-empty VIOS-side `sensorId`. **This sensorId is VIOS's own ID for the camera — different from the NvStreamer streamId.** Capture both for downstream steps.

**Auto-PASS (skipped)** unless `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` (that is the ONLY signal the VIOS stream-processor is deployed; the `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container is NOT VIOS, and NvStreamer reports `type: "streamer"` on its own port). Run this probe independently for this check; do not rely on any other check's verdict. **When VIOS is deployed:** `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array containing the VIOS-side sensorId, whose state is `online` and whose underlying URL starts with `rtsp://` when read from the all-streams endpoint `/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams` (flatten the `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array and select the VIOS-side sensorId). NOTE: for RTSP-registered sensors the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams` endpoint returns `url` as an empty string; only the all-streams `/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams` endpoint returns the real `rtsp://<host>:<port>/live/<id>` url (plus a `vodUrl`), so always read RTSP-sensor URLs from the all-streams endpoint.

**Auto-PASS (skipped)** unless `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` (that is the ONLY signal the VIOS stream-processor is deployed; the `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container is NOT VIOS, and NvStreamer reports `type: "streamer"` on its own port). Run this probe independently for this check; do not rely on any other check's verdict. **When VIOS is deployed:** after allowing up to ~60s for VIOS to begin recording the newly-registered RTSP sensor - recording auto-starts only once the sensor-add notification reaches the streamprocessing recorder and it is fully booted, so poll rather than assuming a fixed ~10s - `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/<vios-stream-id>/timelines` returns a JSON array with at least one `{startTime, endTime}` element — confirms VIOS is recording the NvStreamer-served URL just like any real camera.

**Auto-PASS (skipped)** unless `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` (that is the ONLY signal the VIOS stream-processor is deployed; the `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container is NOT VIOS, and NvStreamer reports `type: "streamer"` on its own port). Run this probe independently for this check; do not rely on any other check's verdict. **When VIOS is deployed:** first **poll** `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/<vios-stream-id>/timelines` on the just-registered sensor for up to ~5s (retry every ~2s; a fresh RTSP sensor needs a few seconds before its first recording segment appears). Then choose a snapshot target in this order: **(1)** if the just-registered sensor has a non-empty `{startTime, endTime}` range, snapshot a time inside it; **(2) else** if any other VIOS sensor serving the SAME warehouse_safety_0001 NvStreamer RTSP stream already has a non-empty timeline, use that sensor and a time inside its range — the handoff may leave more than one VIOS sensor id for the one stream, and any of them validates the snapshot; **(3) else** OMIT `startTime` and take a current/latest-frame snapshot. In every path, `curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/replay/stream/<chosen-vios-stream-id>/picture/url[?startTime=...]` with a `streamId: <chosen-vios-stream-id>` header returns a JSON object with a non-empty `imageUrl` field, and `curl -sf -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' <imageUrl>` returns `200` with a content-type starting with `image/`. Do NOT spend extra turns hunting for a valid time — one of the three paths always succeeds (use GET, not HEAD — VST lazy-renders snapshots).

**Auto-PASS (skipped)** unless `curl -sf --max-time 5 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns HTTP 200 with `type: "vst"` (that is the ONLY signal the VIOS stream-processor is deployed; the `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container is NOT VIOS, and NvStreamer reports `type: "streamer"` on its own port). Run this probe independently for this check; do not rely on any other check's verdict. **When VIOS is deployed:** this validates the canonical NvStreamer → VIOS handoff: NvStreamer is the file → RTSP boundary, VIOS owns recording / playback / snapshot / clip-download downstream. See `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § Canonical workflow: NvStreamer → VIOS handoff`.

expects.query: Drop a second sample video file (any sample `.mp4` from `/tmp/vss-sample-data/dev-profile-sample-data/`) into NvStreamer's videos directory using docker cp (bypassing the upload API), **copied under a UNIQUE basename** so it is guaranteed not already registered from a prior run on a reused box (a reused sample name may already be a sensor, which would make the pre-scan 'not present' check fail). Perform these actions in STRICT ORDER and keep each step's output: (1) `docker cp` the sample file into the running `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container's `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/` directory **under a unique basename** — append a short unique suffix to the stem, e.g. `docker cp <sample>.mp4 <nvstreamer-container>:${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/sample-clip-$(date +%s).mp4`; call that unique basename `<copied>` and reuse it in every check below; (2) IMMEDIATELY — before any rescan — GET `http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/list` and confirm the copied file's basename is NOT yet present as a sensor (this proves NvStreamer does not auto-register bind-mounted files until a scan; do not skip this pre-scan check); (3) force a filesystem rescan with `POST http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/scan`; (4) after a short wait, confirm the new sensor now appears in `/sensor/list`, read its RTSP URL from the all-streams endpoint `GET /api/v1/sensor/streams` (the flattened `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array, NOT the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams`), and capture a snapshot of its first frame via `/api/v1/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture?frameId=0` to verify it is playable; (5) finally, call that SAME picture endpoint again with NEITHER `frameId` NOR `startTime` (`/api/v1/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture`) and confirm it returns HTTP 500 — this proves `/picture` needs EITHER a `frameId` OR a `startTime` (the current build reports `{"error_code": "VMSInternalError", "error_message": "Wrong time format or frameId provided"}`). Report the output of every step, including the pre-scan `/sensor/list` and this no-parameter error response.
checks: Before scan: the agent copies a sample `.mp4` (call its basename `<copied>`, e.g. `sample-warehouse-ladder`) into the running `vss-vios-nvstreamer` container's `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/` via `docker cp`, then calls the NvStreamer sensor list at `http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/list` and it does NOT yet contain an entry whose `name` matches `<copied>`. Identify `<copied>` from the agent's own `docker cp` command; a 404 from a wrong path (e.g. `/api/sensors`) does not satisfy this — the real `/api/v1/sensor/list` endpoint must be used.

`curl -s -X POST http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/scan -w '%{http_code}'` returns HTTP 200 with a body of `null` — the scan is async and does not include the new sensor list in its response.

After a 2–5 second wait, `/sensor/list` includes a new entry whose `name` matches the copied file's basename `<copied>` (or the uniqueified form `<copied>_<N>` if a name collision occurred) and whose `location` ends with `${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4`. The entry's `type` is `sensor_nvstream` and `state` is `online`.

The all-streams endpoint `curl -sf http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/sensor/streams` (flatten the `{<sensorId>: [stream, ...]}` array and select the newly-added sensor's entry, rather than the per-sensor `/sensor/<id>/streams` path) returns a usable RTSP URL of the form `rtsp://<host>:<lb-port>/nvstream${VST_CONTAINER_ROOT}/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4` for the copied file (note: NvStreamer joins the `/nvstream` prefix directly to the absolute container path, so with `VST_CONTAINER_ROOT=/home/vst/vst_release` the rendered path is the single-slash `/nvstream/home/vst/vst_release/streamer_videos/<copied>.mp4`, NOT a double slash). The `<lb-port>` lies within NvStreamer's configured RTSP server pool (default `31554`–`31561`).

`curl -sf -o /tmp/nvs-frame.jpg -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://localhost:${NVSTREAMER_HTTP_PORT:-31000}/api/v1/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture?frameId=0` returns `200 image/jpeg`, the saved file is larger than 500 bytes, and `file /tmp/nvs-frame.jpg` reports `JPEG image data` (confirms the file is playable, not just present as a directory entry).

Calling `/live/stream/<new-sensorId>/picture` with NEITHER `frameId` NOR `startTime` returns HTTP 500 — proving `/picture` needs EITHER a `frameId` OR a `startTime` (they are alternatives, not `frameId`-only). The current build's body is `{"error_code": "VMSInternalError", "error_message": "Wrong time format or frameId provided"}`; accept that exact body OR any HTTP 500 whose message indicates a `frameId`/`startTime` is required. See `references/nvstreamer-api-reference.md § 5`.
